item.title: Lewis Mills shuts out Avon-St. Paul to earn first CIAC football playoff berth
item.description: Lewis Mills/Walcott Tech's Gryfn Kobylarz, 5, tries to get outside during the CIAC high school football game between Avon/St. Paul and Lewis Mills/Walcott Tech. Tuesday, November 24, 2026, Lewis Mills High School, Burlington, Conn. (H John Voorhees III/Hearst Connecticut Media) BURLINGTON – There were a bunch of firsts for the Lewis Mills/Wolcott Tech football co-op team Tuesday: first field goal of the season, first 1,000-yard rusher ever, first 700-yard pass receiver, first eight-victory season. But after a 17-0 shutout of Avon/St. Paul on a frosty evening under portable lights, there was no question what was the biggest first: the first CIAC playoff berth in the 15 years Mills has had a football program. Winners of six straight, the Spartans (8-2) are ranked fifth in Class L and will play their initial postseason game when the CIAC's first round kicks off Dec. 1. The final rankings and pairings will be determined following the Thanksgiving Day games. It's a remarkable turnaround from where Mills was when third-year head coach Jay Pace took over the Spartans. They had just finished a winless season. In his first year, they won one game. A co-op arrangement with Wolcott Tech a year ago brought needed depth and more talent, but the Spartans still won only twice. The school had only had one winning season entering this fall, but the players believed anything was possible. "We set a winning mentality, this senior class. These captains, I love them for that. We set that tone and just continued it from there," tailback Mason Scanlon said. "In the offseason, we were talking playoffs and Coach Pace said, ‘Don't worry about that.' But we knew we had a solid group of guys, and we were going to get it done." Asked if he had thought the playoffs were possible, Pace laughed. "Depends on when you asked me," he replied. "Because of the last couple of years and some of the losses we've had, it was hard to envision we'd be able to turn around our program like we did this year," he added, "but I'm proud of the coaches and players for completely buying into the process. The hard work has paid off." Even when wins were scarce, Pace could chalk up little victories, such as better practice habits or closer ballgames with the team competing into the fourth quarter, instead of getting blown out by mercy rule. On the sidelines, the team also brought in four new assistant coaches this fall, a welcome addition. As the wins piled up, the team's mentality changed. That was apparent Tuesday following the opening kickoff, when Avon's Peyton Bip bobbled the ball, then bolted all the way to the Mills 25 to put the Spartans in an immediate jam. "In the past, that momentum swing would've been hard for us to overcome," Pace said. Not this time. On Avon's first play, Mills defensive end Nate Bertand sacked Avon QB Christian Wankier for a 1-yard loss. After an incomplete pass, a 1-yard pass play and another incompletion, Mills had halted the Falcons' scoring threat in its tracks. "

item.description: Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images How did Jayson Tatum remain even-keeled during Celtics’ losing streak? Experience appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . There was some panic regarding the Boston Celtics after they had lost three consecutive games , all of which were close. There was a noticeable trend in each one of those losses to the Denver Nuggets, Sacramento Kings, and Golden State Warriors — their offense lost steam late in games, perhaps due to their purported overreliance on the jumpshot. But on Tuesday, with Jayson Tatum and Paul George both suiting up in NBA Cup action against the Washington Wizards, the Celtics bounced back in a big way. It looked like the Wizards were going to keep the same story running for Boston, but in the end, the Celtics found their footing, held off a hard charge from Washington, and put an end to their losing skid with a 131-116 victory. There are plenty of ebbs and flows throughout the course of the 82-game NBA regular season, and Tatum, being in his 10th season already in the association, knows better than to panic when things aren’t going the Celtics’ way. We can only focus on today,” Tatum told NBC’s Zora Stephenson in his postgame interview. “It’s in my 10th year. Boston would not look back after this mini spurt and would win by 15 points in the end. If there’s a silver lining to the Celtics’ recent slump, it’s that it happened early in the season and they can address the issues that came up during that three-game losing streak to prevent them from coming up again, especially when the games matter the most. item.title: UWM Panthers respond well to challenge No. 3 Florida
item.description: Three days after falling flat against a beatable opponent, the UW-Milwaukee Panthers gave one of the best men’s college basketball teams in the country a run for its money. Led by senior forward Chandler Jackson , the Panthers hung with third-ranked Florida into the final minutes before suffering a 76-67 loss Nov. 24 at Tower Hill Arena in Gainesville, Florida . The game was tied 48-48 with 13 minutes left and the Panthers (2-5) were within five with 2 ½ minutes to play against the Gators (7-1), who had been ranked No. 1 until the Nov. 23 poll. The performance followed the worst loss of the season for Milwaukee, which fell to St. Thomas by 28 points Nov. 21 at the UWM Panther Arena. Box score: Florida 76, Milwaukee 67 "I thought they responded well from the other night, not only in practice and our preparation, but also just the fight that we had on the court tonight," said UWM coach Bart Lundy , who had ripped his team’s competitiveness after the loss to St. Thomas. "And that was really what we wanted, was to come out of this game knowing that everybody in this building saw a hard-playing team, and I think that's what they saw." Jackson made three consecutive 3-pointers as the Panthers closed the Gators’ biggest gap of the night to within 72-67. Jackson finished with 20 points, including four 3-pointers. UWM shot 10 for 19 (52.6%) from 3-point range and 26 for 59 (44.1%) overall. Junior forward Al Amadou went 5 for 5 on his way to a career-high 13 points, and senior forward Danilo Jovanovich added 11 points and four assists. Senior guard Tre Norman , like Amadou a transfer from Marquette, finished with eight points, eight rebounds and four assists. Florida was led by senior center Rueben Chinyelu , who scored a career-high 25 points and grabbed 16 rebounds. "We really wanted to win that game, but we're getting better as a team," Lundy said. "We tied it late but had a little stretch where we didn't possess the ball as well as we had, and they got out on a break. But I thought our guys stuck to the game plan and they really competed. And that's got to be the standard all the time. If we can compete in this environment, we can compete anywhere." UWM is back on the road against 8-0 Oregon State at 1 p.m. Nov. 29 in Corvalis, Oregon. item.title: Jamari Phillips’ Late Heroics Lift WSU Past Sam Houston
item.description: PALM DESERT, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 21: Jamari Phillips #33 of the Washington State Cougars reacts to a call in the second half of an Acrisure Series men's college basketball tournament game between the Duke Blue Devils and the Washington State Cougars at Acrisure Arena on November 21, 2026 in Palm Desert, California. (Photo by Greg Fiore/Getty Images) | Getty Images In the first-ever men’s basketball meeting between the schools, a strong finish over the final two minutes pushed Washington State (3-4) past Sam Houston (3-4), 80-73. With the game tied at 70 with 1:20 remaining, Sam Houston had possession and was threatening to take the lead. After a corner 3-pointer missed everything, Tyler Kropp was called for a loose-ball foul while boxing out for a rebound. Sam Houston’s Riccardo Greppi went to the line for a one-and-one with a chance to put his team ahead. Greppi missed the free throw, but the Bearkats secured the offensive rebound for another opportunity to take the lead. The Cougar defense held strong, forcing a turnover and giving WSU another chance to take a late lead. Lazerek Houston brought the ball up the court, with Kropp setting a screen at the top of the key. Houston drove left before turning and passing the ball back to Jamari Phillips near the Cougar logo. Phillips took one dribble to his left before rising up and drilling a 3-pointer while drawing a foul. Jamari Phillips!! From deep again!! You did not!! #GoCougs | #NextIsNow pic.twitter.com/OXtadH8Bsm — Washington State Men's Basketball (@WSUCougarsMBB) November 25, 2026 After converting the free throw, Phillips gave the Cougars a four-point lead with 30 seconds remaining. Sam Houston wasn’t going away quietly, however. Justin Begg quickly brought the ball up the court and knocked down a three-pointer to cut the WSU lead back down to one. After a quick inbound pass, Phillips found himself at the free-throw line again, where he knocked down both attempts to extend the Cougar lead to three. On the ensuing possession, Sam Houston had two opportunities to tie the game but missed both shots. The rebound fell to, you guessed it, Phillips, who was fouled and sent to the line with another opportunity to seal the game. Phillips came through again, knocking down both free throws to push the Cougar lead to five and secure the 80-73 victory. It was a solid win for the Cougars, who have now won three of their last four games. Their only loss during that stretch was a four-point defeat against No. 16 Duke. Sam Houston entered the game with a notable win over a Pac-12 opponent, having defeated Boise State by 14 points Friday. WSU will close out its two-game homestand Friday with a matchup against Palouse foe Idaho at 5 p.m. The Cougars will then travel to Kentucky to face Murray State on Monday.

item.description: 'I can play all three formats!' Vaibhav Sooryavanshi reveals Yuvraj Singh's game-changing advice after smashing 204 vs UAE originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has revealed that a phone call with Yuvraj Singh changed his approach vs UAE. A rare lean patch in Doha had left the teenager searching for answers. Several world records fell as India A booked a semi-final place in Doha. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi credits Yuvraj Singh after 52-ball list a double century vs UAE in Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is convinced that he can adapt to Test cricket, one-day internationals and T20Is alike, especially after being empowered with pearls of wisdom from his idol Yuvraj Singh. He made 204 off only 53 balls, reaching the double hundred in 52 deliveries with the help of seven fours and 28 sixes at a strike rate of 384.90 against UAE to help India A chase down 250 in just 14.2 overs, which secured a semi-final place in the ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026. What made the performance more special was that he came into the match on the back of a slump, after managing only a handful of runs in the tournament and in domestic cricket before that. He was worried enough to seek advice from several people close to him, including his childhood idol Yuvraj Singh, and a long phone conversation with the former all-rounder appears to have changed his thinking. Troubled by his run of low scores, Sooryavanshi spoke to four people on the eve of the match, namely his father, his childhood coach Manish Ojha, his Under-19 teammate Pratham Janchak and Yuvraj. "Yesterday I spoke to four people, only four people," he said in an interview with the BCCI. "He told me a lot of things and explained things to me about batting. Yuvraj "explained everything thoroughly for half an hour" and gave him a simple target, which was that the score would be different if he batted through 20 balls. item.title: Josh Allen explains why facing Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs feels different now
item.description: Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images Josh Allen has admitted that facing Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs has become an annual fixture in his NFL career, with the Buffalo Bills quarterback now comparing the matchup to an AFC East divisional game. The Bills are preparing to host Kansas City in another major showdown between two of the AFC’s leading quarterbacks. Their regular meetings have helped establish one of the NFL’s most recognisable rivalries. This will be the 11th meeting between the two teams since 2020, with the previous 10 encounters split evenly at five wins apiece. Josh Allen compares Kansas City Chiefs rivalry to an AFC East divisional game Speaking about the upcoming matchup, Allen acknowledged how frequently the Bills and Chiefs have faced each other throughout his career. “This is one that seems like it’s on the books every year,” Allen said. “At this point, it’s almost a division game.” The quarterback’s comments reflect just how familiar the two organisations have become with one another. Although Kansas City are not a divisional opponent, their repeated meetings have given the fixture a similar feel. Buffalo won the most recent regular-season meeting between the sides, claiming a 28-21 victory after Allen led the Bills past the Chiefs. Mahomes will now have an opportunity to respond as the teams prepare for another important encounter. Both quarterbacks have also been productive during the current campaign. Allen enters Week 12 with 2,527 passing yards, 290 rushing yards and 25 total touchdowns, including 14 through the air and 11 on the ground. He has also thrown nine interceptions while completing 64.2 per cent of his passes. Mahomes has recorded 2,709 passing yards, 22 touchdowns and four interceptions through 10 games. The Chiefs quarterback has completed 67.1 per cent of his attempts while adding 100 rushing yards and a touchdown. With the series level at five wins apiece since 2020, the latest meeting offers another chance for either quarterback to take the advantage in a rivalry that has become a regular feature of the NFL calendar. item.title: Iowa Still On The Outside Looking In At College Football Playoff
item.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Iowa moved up to 13th, but the Hawkeyes remain hopeful heading into regular season finale vs. Nebraska. One of the biggest Iowa football games in program history is set for Black Friday. The Hawkeyes found out that they are still on the outside looking in at a spot in the College Football Playoff. The committee revealed that they have Iowa 13th, two spots from being included in the playoffs. Related: Iowa State Star Aiden Flora, The Nation’s Leading Rusher, Announces His Future Plans Currently, the Hawkeyes are the second team left out, as Oregon sits 12th. Boise State, who dropped out of the Top 25, is in as the highest-ranked team from the non-Power 4 conferences. That, despite a recent loss to San Diego State. Regardless, Iowa still needs to take care of business. Nebraska Is Not Going To Just Rollover For The Hawkeyes Not only is this one of the biggest rivalry games for both schools, but the Huskers moved into the latest College Football Playoff rankings at No. 25 this week. Now, they not only have something to play for themselves, but can absolutely ruin things for Iowa in the process. Related: Ohio State Staring In The Face Of A Fifth Loss With Michigan Coming Up Dating back to 1891, Nebraska leads the series all-time, 30-23-3. Since becoming a trophy game, it has been all Iowa, with the Hawkeyes taking 11 of 15, including each of the last three. Of those three, the first two were 13-10 wins for Iowa. The most recent, though, was one of the biggest wins in the series in recent memory, 40-16. The Hawkeyes also won by 42 back in 2017 in Lincoln. Iowa Is Going To Still Need Help Would a win by the Hawkeyes allow them to leap Oregon? The committee has yet to show they are willing to do just that. Texas Tech, BYU and UCLA hold spots just ahead of Iowa and the Ducks. UCLA has been incredible this year, suffering just one loss. Same for Texas Tech, with BYU sitting at two. Oregon is the highest-ranked three-loss team, with USC being next at No. 15. First and foremost for the Hawkeyes must be taking care of business. The 40-year-old, however, failed to make much of a mark. In that limited time in the big leagues, he put up a horrid OPS of .279 after recording just two hits in 24 at-bats. item.description: It was the rock band Dire Straits who immortalized the phrase “money for nothing," but it’s college athletics that now wears it as a motto. Here in Michigan, our largest state university has just bungled its dealings with Trev Alberts, an athletic director candidate from Texas A&M who was reportedly told he had the Michigan job last week – and was then told over the weekend he does not . Immediately, Alberts and his lawyers (because there are always lawyers) produced a memorandum of understanding that allegedly binds Michigan to the deal or else pays Alberts $17.2 million to walk away from it . Wait – $17.2 million? SHAWN WINDSOR: U-M's latest dysfunctional mess might save its football coach This in addition to $4 million Michigan would owe Texas A&M for Alberts' buyout, which I suppose covers their enormous pain and suffering for a weekend’s worth of thinking they have to find a new AD. The Bulldogs enter today at 3-1, with their lone loss coming on a buzzer-beater in what was technically a neutral-site matchup in Spokane, WA. They beat Purdue 78-72 to open the season, and did so in the same building as tonight’s contest. Their other two wins came on their home floor, as like most major teams they don’t need to travel away from home expect to play other big-name programs. Somewhat surprisingly, K-State is 3-1 all time against Gonzaga, with all four matchups coming in the last 32 years, and the lone win for the Bulldogs coming on a neutral court in Seattle in 2012 in Bruce Weber’s first season. K-State returned to the win column the next season in Wichita, and the two programs haven’t played since. If they squad that took out Creighton shows up, this could be a very interesting game. item.description: Dalton Kincaid expects to play. Getty Dalton Kincaid expects to play against the Chiefs. Getty The Buffalo Bills are expected to have star tight end Dalton Kincaid on the field on Thursday. Buffalo is coming off a lopsided win over the Miami Dolphins to improve to 9-1 and remains atop the AFC, as the Bills control their own destiny to the No. 1 seed in the AFC. Buffalo will host the Kansas City Chiefs on Thursday night on Thanksgiving. Dalton Kincaid Breaks Silence on Injury Status Getty Dalton Kincaid expects to play against the Chiefs. The Bills were without starting tight end Dalton Kincaid against the Miami Dolphins due to an injury, and his status against the Chiefs was up in the air. Kincaid was considered a limited participant in practice on Tuesday, yet he told reporters he expects to play on Thursday. Dalton Kincaid just now: “I’ll be there Thursday. I’m most likely playing.” — Matt Parrino (@MattParrino) November 24, 2026 “I’ll be there Thursday. I’m most likely playing,” Kincaid said to reporters, according to Matt Parrino. Getting Kincaid back would be a major addition to the Bills’ offense. Although he hasn’t had much of a role on offense over the last few weeks, he is another weapon the Chiefs have to guard and game plan for, especially up the middle. item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Gotham FC’s home semifinal moved to 5K-seat stadium in field quality debacle
item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
